subject: DeltaAI — private GPU pool capacity & cost mapping
messages:
From: Sachin Patel <sachin.patel@deltaai.com>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@deltaai.com
Date: Sun, 02 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Capacity kickoff — private GPU pool for DeltaAI

Hi Lukas,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. We're moving forward with a private deployment of Redwood in our us-west-2 VPC (dedicated crossconnect planned) and need an initial capacity plan to share with procurement and infra. High level:

- Sustained target: ~2,500 inference QPS (model: open-llama-7b equivalent)
- Expected request mix: ~70% chat-style (avg tokens ~60), 30% embedding/rerank (shorter sequences)
- Peak surges: up to ~12,000 QPS for short windows (5–15 minutes) during business-critical batch jobs
- Latency target: P95 <= 150ms for chat flows (with fallback to lower-capacity model at severe load)
- Data residency: traffic must stay within our VPC; egress budget is constrained

I've attached a CSV with our 30-day sample traffic (deltaai_workload_profile.csv) and our formal SLO doc (SLO_requirements.pdf). Can your team:

1) Propose a sizing (sustained pool + burst/warm pool) with rough cost estimate
2) Call out networking constraints (egress, crossconnect sizing, QoS) and any recommended admission-control rules
3) Estimate warm-cache strategies and model quantization tradeoffs

Can we set a 45-min design call this week? 

Thanks,
Sachin Patel
Head of Platform
DeltaAI

Attachments: deltaai_workload_profile.csv; SLO_requirements.pdf

From: Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 05 May 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: DeltaAI capacity — initial sizing draft and ask for simulation

Team — forwarding the thread from DeltaAI. Key constraints: sustained 2.5k QPS baseline, 12k QPS short spikes, P95 <=150ms target, A100 preferred. Sachin provided 99th token ~480.

Initial thinking (very rough):
- Primary pool (sustained): 6–8 A100-equivalent nodes with conservative batching and aggressive KV/prefix caching. This should hit ~2.5k sustained QPS assuming model quantization to int8 and sequence mix provided.
- Burst/warm pool: 8–12 nodes reserved for short spikes with warm KV caches (warm-up strategy: keep <30% warm cache resident across a subset of nodes to reduce cold-start token cost). Autoscale to burst nodes via an admission controller that triggers at 85% sustained CPU/GPU utilization or when queueing latency > 80ms.
- Admission control: prioritize chat traffic; embed/rerank flows can be deprioritized or rate-limited during spikes
- Network: recommend dedicated crossconnect with minimum 100Gbps aggregate, with QoS shaping per lane (chat priority) and per-node egress limit ~15 Gbps to support KV & sharded model IO.
- Cost order-of-magnitude: sustained pool + burst reservation looks like $xxk–$yyk/month depending on instance type and crossconnect cost (I'll add numbers after simulation).

Actions: Karthik — can you run a batch simulation with the attached sample CSV (deltaai_workload_profile.csv) + the token distribution Sachin shared and return: per-node QPS, rendezvous latency, and warm-cache hit-rate estimates? Use both float16 and int8 quantized variants.
Marissa — can you capture realistic procurement lead times for 6 / 12 A100s in us-west-2 (including crossconnect provisioning) and map to a mutual action plan?

Attachment: deltaai_initial_sizing.xlsx

Thanks,
Lukas

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 08 May 2027 10:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: DeltaAI capacity — initial sizing draft and ask for simulation

Lukas / team — ran the sims (attached summary). Key findings:

- Float16 baseline: each A100-equivalent node sustains ~420 QPS for the chat workload (avg seq 60) with P95 ~ 130–170ms depending on batching window. To reach 2.5k sustained, we need ~6 nodes (6*420=2520) but margin is thin for cache-miss paths.
- Int8 quant (aggressive): per-node throughput increases ~1.8x (est. ~760 QPS/node) with P95 ~ 140ms; however, tail variance increases under cold-cache conditions.
- Warm-cache strategy: maintaining a small warm lane (20–30% of active sessions pinned to a hot subset) reduces tail penalty. With warm cache, 6 int8 nodes comfortably hit sustained target with 2–3 node buffer for failover.
- Burst handling: for 12k spikes, we recommend a 10-node burst pool (quantized models) with pre-warmed KV. Autoscale cold-start to burst nodes takes ~70–110s depending on image pull and cache hydration — pre-warming via a rolling keep-warm policy reduces visible latency.
- Network: observed egress per node during peak is ~12–18 Gbps when serving high embedding rates; recommend 100Gbps crossconnect and per-node QoS to prevent noisy-neighbor egress saturation.

Recommendations:
1) Primary pool: 6 int8-quantized A100-equivalent nodes with a 2-node buffer for failover (operational target: 8 physical nodes allocated).
2) Burst/warm pool: 10 nodes reserved, with warm-keep percentage ~25% and an admission controller that sheds non-critical embed flows at 85% GPU util.
3) Autoscale policy: aggressive warm-keep + pre-pull images; scale-up cooldown 45s; scale-up full readiness 90s.

Estimated month run-rate (infrastructure + basic support): $58,000 — $82,000 depending on crossconnect pricing and reserved vs on-demand transient burst capacity. Detailed numbers in karthik_simulation_summary.csv.

I can flesh out the node-level perf matrices if we want to show this to procurement.

-Karthik
Senior Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: karthik_simulation_summary.csv

From: Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwood.ai>

Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, procurement@deltaai.com, onprem-support@ironstack.io
Date: Sat, 08 May 2027 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal: DeltaAI private GPU pool — sizing, network, and MAP

Sachin — thanks for the data and the call. Based on our simulations and follow-ups, here is a concise proposal and Mutual Action Plan (MAP):

Summary of recommendation:
- Primary (sustained) pool: 6 A100-equivalent nodes running int8-quantized models, with 2-node failover buffer (allocate 8 nodes total to procurement)
- Burst/warm pool: 10 reserved nodes, warm-keep ~25% (pre-warm KV/cache lanes), auto-scale policy to bring burst capacity online within ~90s of trigger
- Network: 100Gbps crossconnect, per-node QoS, per-node egress budget ~15 Gbps; NAT for control plane only (no customer data egress)
- Admission control: prioritize chat; shed embed/rerank under sustained 85% GPU util; fallback to smaller model under extreme saturation
- Cost run-rate: estimated $58k–$82k / month (breakdown attached) — depends on reserved discount and crossconnect costs

Immediate MAP (owners & deadlines):
- DeltaAI: confirm procurement approval to allocate 8 A100-equivalent instances & approve 100Gbps crossconnect by 2027-05-20 (owner: procurement@deltaai.com)
- Redwood (Marissa): provide procurement SOW and lead times for node reservation by 2027-05-13
- Redwood (Karthik): provide detailed per-node perf matrices + cold/warm cache hit assumptions by 2027-05-12
- Joint: 1 week staging run to validate warm-keep and admission-control behavior (target: 2027-06-01 start)

Next steps: please review and call out any constraints (cost ceiling, procurement windows, regulatory checks). If this looks good, we'll prepare a short SOW and schedule the staging run kick-off.

Thanks — happy to jump on a follow-up with procurement and infra.

Best,
Lukas Meyer
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Attachments: deltaai_initial_sizing.xlsx; karthik_simulation_summary.csv
